Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Yes! MapLibre ships a **style-spec validator** that you can run from the command line.  
It will parse your exported Mapbox style JSON, check it against the MapLibre Style Specification, and report any properties, source URLs, sprite/glyph references, or syntax that aren’t supported.

### 1. Install the validator (dev-dependency)

```bash
# From the root of your project
npm install --save-dev @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
```

> The package contains the same validator that powers the online “Validate style” button in Maputnik, but it works offline and can be scripted into CI.

### 2. Run the CLI

```bash
# Basic usage – validates `style.json` and prints a human-readable report
npx gl-style-validate path/to/style.json
```

**Typical output**

```
✔ style.json is a valid MapLibre style (v8)

⚠ 1 warning
  - source "my-tiles" uses a Mapbox URL (mapbox://…) – replace with a public or self-hosted source

✖ 2 errors
  - layer "road-label" references source-layer "road_label" which does not exist in source "my-tiles"
  - sprite URL "mapbox://sprites/…" is not reachable – provide a PNG/JSON sprite bundle
```

The exit code is `0` when the style passes validation, non-zero otherwise, so you can fail a CI job automatically.

### 3. Options you may find handy

| Flag | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `--quiet` | Suppress the “✔ valid” line – only errors/warnings are printed. |
| `--output json` | Emit a JSON object (`{valid:…, errors:…, warnings:…}`) – useful for scripts. |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as errors (exit code 1). |
| `--help` | Show the full help text. |

Example for CI:

```bash
npx gl-style-validate --strict --output json style.json > style-validation.json
```

### 4. What the validator checks (and what it **doesn’t**)

| ✅ Checked by the validator | ❌ Not checked (you still need to test) |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| JSON syntax & required top-level fields (`version`, `sources`, `layers`, `glyphs`, `sprite`) | Whether the URLs you point to actually serve tiles (CORS, auth, 401) |
| Correct `source` and `source-layer` names against the declared sources | Compatibility of custom expressions that rely on Mapbox-only functions (e.g., `["image", …]` with Mapbox-hosted images) |
| Presence of required `type` values for each layer (`fill`, `line`, `symbol`, …) | Runtime performance issues (e.g., too many layers, heavy filters) |
| Valid `sky`/`terrain` objects (MapLibre-specific) | Whether your custom fonts are available in the `glyphs` endpoint |

If the validator reports **only warnings** about Mapbox URLs, you’ll need to replace those URLs with equivalents (e.g., a public vector tile service, a self-hosted sprite, or an OpenStreetMap-based glyphs endpoint). After fixing the warnings, run the validator again until it reports a clean pass.

### 5. Quick visual sanity-check (optional)

Even after a successful CLI run, it’s a good idea to open the style in **Maputnik**:

```bash
npx maputnik
```

- Drag-and-drop your `style.json` into the editor.
- The UI will highlight any missing sprites/glyphs and let you edit source URLs on the fly.
- You can also export the corrected JSON directly from Maputnik.

### 6. Putting it into a typical workflow

```bash
# 1️⃣ Export style from Mapbox Studio → style.json
# 2️⃣ Run validator locally
npx gl-style-validate style.json

# 3️⃣ If warnings → edit style.json (replace mapbox:// URLs, adjust source-layer names)
# 4️⃣ Re-run validator until it passes
# 5️⃣ Commit the final style and push to production
# 6️⃣ (CI) Add a step that fails the build if validation fails
```

### TL;DR

- **CLI tool:** `npx gl-style-validate <style-file>`
- **Install:** `npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`
- **Use:** Run it locally or in CI; fix any reported errors/warnings (especially stray `mapbox://` URLs) before deploying.
- **Optional visual check:** `npx maputnik` to edit and re-export.

That’s all you need to verify that your exported Mapbox style JSON is compatible with MapLibre before you ship it. Happy mapping!

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **step-by-step recipe** you can copy-paste into a fresh project to see a working MapLibre map **without any API key**. It uses a public, open-source style that already points at free vector tiles, sprites and glyphs, so you can verify that the rest of your migration (namespace changes, CSS, etc.) is correct before you wire up your own tiles. --- ## 1️⃣ Quick “does it work?” test ```html MapLibre test – no token
``` ### What this does | Piece | Why it matters for a token-free test | |------|--------------------------------------| | **`style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json'`** | This is the official MapLibre demo style. It references **OpenMapTiles** vector tiles (`https://demotiles.maplibre.org/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`), a public sprite (`.../sprite.png`) and glyphs (`.../glyphs/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`). No `mapbox://` URLs, no token. | | **`import * as maplibregl …`** | Uses the ESM build (v6+). No default export, so the `* as` syntax is required. | | **`map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl())`** | Shows that the control CSS class (`maplibregl-ctrl`) works out-of-the-box. | Open the file in a browser (or serve it with a simple static server, e.g. `npx serve .`). You should see a fully rendered map. If you do, the **migration basics are correct** – the next steps are just swapping in your own style/tile source. --- ## 2️⃣ If you want a style that looks more like Mapbox’s “Streets” The demo style is a good sanity check, but you may prefer a style that resembles Mapbox’s default “streets” or “outdoors”. Two ready-made, token-free options are: | Name | Style URL | What it uses | |------|-----------|--------------| | **OpenFreeMap – Liberty** | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` | Vector tiles from OpenFreeMap (OSM-derived), sprite & glyphs hosted on the same domain. | | **OpenMapTiles – Basic** | `https://tiles.openmaptiles.org/styles/osm-bright/style.json` | Vector tiles from the OpenMapTiles demo server, with a classic “OSM Bright” look. | Just replace the `style` line in the snippet above with one of those URLs. ```js style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // or the OSM-Bright URL ``` > **Tip:** If you open the style URL in a browser you’ll see the raw JSON. It’s a perfect starting point for editing with **Maputnik** (see §4). --- ## 3️⃣ What you need to change in your existing code | Old Mapbox piece | New MapLibre piece | Why | |------------------|--------------------|-----| | `mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.…'` | **Remove it** | MapLibre never reads `accessToken`. | | `style: 'mapbox://styles/…'` | `style: ''` | `mapbox://` URLs point to Mapbox-hosted resources that require a token. | | `mapboxgl` namespace | `maplibregl` | All constructors, constants, and static methods moved. | | CSS classes like `mapboxgl-ctrl` | `maplibregl-ctrl` | The CSS file shipped with MapLibre uses the new prefix. | | `map.loadImage(url, cb)` | `const {data} = await map.loadImage(url)` | From v4.0.0 onward MapLibre returns a promise. | | `map.setFog(...)` | `map.setSky(...)` (or skip) | Fog is a Mapbox-v2-only API; MapLibre uses the `sky` layer instead. | If you have **custom style JSON** that you exported from Mapbox Studio, you’ll need to: 1. **Replace every `url` that starts with `mapbox://`** (tiles, sprites, glyphs) with a URL that points at your new tile source. 2. **Adjust source-layer names** if the new vector tile schema uses different names (e.g., `road` → `transportation`). 3. **Validate** the edited JSON with the CLI: ```bash npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec npx gl-style-validate my-style.json ``` Fix any errors before feeding the style to the map. --- ## 4️⃣ Editing the style (optional but handy) If you want to tweak colors, add/remove layers, or simply see the style in a UI: 1. Open the style URL in **Maputnik** – the online editor at https://maputnik.github.io/editor/. 2. Paste the JSON (or load it via the URL field). 3. Change the `sources` section to point at your chosen tile service, e.g.: ```json "sources": { "openfreemap": { "type": "vector", "url": "pmtiles://https://tiles.openfreemap.org/tiles.pmtiles" } } ``` 4. Click **Export → Download** and replace the old style file in your project (or host the edited JSON somewhere reachable). --- ## 5️⃣ Common “blank map” pitfalls (quick checklist) | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **Map loads but is completely gray** | Style still contains a `mapbox://` sprite, glyphs, or source URL. | Search the whole JSON for `mapbox://` and replace. | | **Only the background shows, no roads/labels** | Source-layer names don’t match the new vector tile schema. | Open the tile source’s documentation (e.g., OpenFreeMap) and update `source-layer` values in your style. | | **CORS error in console** | Tile server doesn’t allow cross-origin requests from your domain. | Use a tile provider that sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (most public demo servers do) or proxy the tiles. | | **`401` / `403` HTTP error** | A stray Mapbox token is still being sent (e.g., in a plugin). | Remove any `accessToken` usage from plugins, or replace the plugin with a MapLibre-compatible version. | | **`map.setFog is not a function`** | You still have Mapbox v2 fog code. | Delete it or replace with `map.setSky({…})`. | --- ## 6️⃣ Plug-in checklist (if you use any) | Mapbox plugin you might have | MapLibre equivalent / notes | |------------------------------|-----------------------------| | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` | Works **as-is** after you change the CSS prefix (`mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`). See the MapLibre example: https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/examples/draw-polygon-with-mapbox-gl-draw/ | | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` | Replace with `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` (or any other geocoder UI) and point it at Nominatim / MapTiler Geocoding. | | `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions` | Replace with `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions` (works with any OSRM-compatible service). | | `mapbox-gl-compare` | Use `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-compare`. | | Any plugin that hard-codes `mapboxgl` in its source or CSS | Fork it or open an issue on the repo; many plugins have already been updated for MapLibre. | If you’re not sure which plugins you have, grep your source tree for `mapboxgl` or `@mapbox/` and list them. Then run each through the table above. --- ## 7️⃣ Full “real-world” example (using OpenFreeMap) ```javascript import * as maplibregl from 'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@^6.0.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs'; import MapLibreGeocoder from '@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder'; // npm install @maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder import '@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder/dist/maplibre-gl-geocoder.css'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // token-free style center: [13.405, 52.52], // Berlin zoom: 12, }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl(), 'top-left'); // Add a geocoder that talks to the public Nominatim instance const geocoder = new MapLibreGeocoder({ placeholder: 'Search Berlin…', // Nominatim endpoint (public demo, not for production) url: 'https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search', // optional: limit results, add viewbox, etc. }); map.addControl(geocoder, 'top-right'); ``` *Run the above after `npm i @maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` (or use a CDN import). The map will render, and the search box will work against the free Nominatim service.* --- ## 8️⃣ Next steps after the test passes 1. **Pick a production-grade tile source** – e.g., self-hosted OpenMapTiles, a commercial provider like MapTiler Cloud, or PMTiles on S3. 2.

Description: anti-pattern — assuming Mapbox v2 features work in MapLibre
prompt: I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including placing the camera at a given longitude, latitude and altitude. After migrating to MapLibre, that code is broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### What happened? `map.setFreeCameraOptions()` / `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` are **Mapbox-GL-JS v2-only** APIs. MapLibre GL JS never implemented the “free-camera” class, so after you swapped the package and the namespace the call simply does not exist (`map.setFreeCameraOptions is not a function`). You didn’t do anything wrong – you just hit a feature that **doesn’t exist in MapLibre**. The migration guide (step 4) tells you how to achieve the same effect with the MapLibre API. --- ## How to place the camera at a specific **longitude, latitude, altitude** in MapLibre 1. **Calculate the CameraOptions** that describe the desired view. MapLibre provides two helper methods that turn a “free-camera” description into the standard `CameraOptions` object (`center`, `zoom`, `pitch`, `bearing`, `elevation`, `roll`). ```js // lng/lat of the camera position const camLngLat = [lon, lat]; // e.g. [-122.42, 37.78] // altitude in meters above the ellipsoid (or above ground if you have terrain) const camAlt = 500; // metres // optional orientation const bearing = 30; // degrees clockwise from north const pitch = 45; // degrees from horizontal const roll = 0; // rarely used // v5.0+ helper – returns a CameraOptions object const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( camLngLat, // [lon, lat] camAlt, // altitude (m) bearing, // bearing (°) pitch, // pitch (°) roll // roll (°) – optional ); ``` *If you are on an older MapLibre (v2-v4) you can use the older helper:* ```js const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromTo( camLngLat, camAlt, // “from” position camLngLat, camAlt, // “to” – same point if you just want a static view bearing, pitch, roll ); ``` 2. **Apply the options** with any of the standard camera-movement methods (`jumpTo`, `easeTo`, `flyTo`). Choose the one that matches the animation you want. ```js // Instant jump (no animation) map.jumpTo(camOpts); // Smooth animated move // map.easeTo(camOpts); // or map.flyTo(camOpts); ``` The `camOpts` object already contains `center`, `zoom`, `pitch`, `bearing`, **`elevation`** (the altitude you supplied) and optionally `roll`. ### Full example (MapLibre v6) ```js import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // any non-Mapbox style center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12 }); map.on('load', () => { // Desired free-camera pose const lngLat = [-122.42, 37.78]; const altitude = 800; // metres above sea level / terrain const bearing = 45; // degrees const pitch = 60; // degrees const roll = 0; // optional // Compute the CameraOptions that MapLibre understands const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( lngLat, altitude, bearing, pitch, roll ); // Move the view – choose jump/ease/fly map.jumpTo(camOpts); // no animation // map.easeTo(camOpts); // smooth pan/zoom }); ``` --- ## Quick checklist – did you miss any other migration steps? | Step | What to verify | Typical symptom if missed | |------|----------------|---------------------------| | **1. Package & import** | `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl`
Import with `import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'` (or `{Map}`) | “mapboxgl is not defined” or missing CSS | | **2. Namespace** | Replace **all** `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl` (including CSS class prefixes `mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`) | Controls appear unstyled, runtime errors | | **3. Access token & style URL** | Remove `mapboxgl.accessToken`; use a style that does **not** start with `mapbox://` (e.g. OpenFreeMap, your own TileJSON style) | Blank map, `401/403` errors, “mapbox://” in console | | **4. API differences** | • Callbacks → promises (`loadImage`, cluster methods)
• v2-only methods (`setFog`, `setFreeCameraOptions`, `getFreeCameraOptions`) → MapLibre equivalents (`setSky`, `calculateCameraOptions…`) | “is not a function” errors | | **5. Plugins** | Replace Mapbox-only plugins (`@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder`, `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions`) with their MapLibre forks (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions`) or other open alternatives. | Missing controls, 401 from Mapbox APIs | | **6. Behaviour changes** | • `map.on(...).on(...)` chaining no longer works (v5)
• Canvas context attributes moved under `canvasContextAttributes`
• WebGL2 is now required (v6) | Errors on map construction, missing features | If you’ve already taken care of steps 1-3 and only the free-camera code is broken, the snippet above should fix it. --- ## TL;DR *Mapbox’s `setFreeCameraOptions` does not exist in MapLibre.* Use `map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(...)` (or the older `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo`) to build a `CameraOptions` object, then call `map.jumpTo`, `map.easeTo`, or `map.flyTo`. Make sure the rest of the migration checklist (package, namespace, style URL, token removal, plugin replacements) is also satisfied, and your map should work exactly as before—just with an open-source stack. If you run into any other specific errors, let me know which plugin or API you’re using and I can give a more targeted fix.
